q: Identify the term described as “Software embedded in hardware”.
e: Firmware: Software embedded in hardware. Provides low-level control

q: Identify the term described as “Basic Input/Output System”.
e: BIOS: Basic Input/Output System. Initializes hardware during boot on traditional PCs

q: Identify the term described as “Unified Extensible Firmware Interface”.
e: UEFI: Unified Extensible Firmware Interface. Modern replacement for legacy BIOS

q: Identify the term described as “Process of starting a computer and loading the operating system”.
e: Booting: Process of starting a computer and loading the operating system. Can be cold or warm

q: Identify the term described as “Named collection of data”.
e: File: Named collection of data. Stored on a file system

q: Identify the term described as “Container used to organize files and subfolders”.
e: Folder: Container used to organize files and subfolders. Also called a directory

q: Identify the term described as “Suffix indicating file type or format”.
e: File extension: Suffix indicating file type or format. Examples include .txt and .jpg

q: Identify the term described as “Organized collection of related data”.
e: Database: Organized collection of related data. Managed by a database system

q: Identify the term described as “Database Management System”.
e: DBMS: Database Management System. Creates, stores, queries and controls databases

q: Identify the term described as “Finite sequence of steps for solving a problem”.
e: Algorithm: Finite sequence of steps for solving a problem. Must be unambiguous and terminate

q: Identify the term described as “Set of instructions executed by a computer”.
e: Program: Set of instructions executed by a computer. Written in a programming language

q: Identify the term described as “Human-readable program instructions”.
e: Source code: Human-readable program instructions. Translated or interpreted for execution

q: Identify the term described as “Program translating source code into machine or intermediate code”.
e: Compiler: Program translating source code into machine or intermediate code. Typically processes a whole program

q: Identify the term described as “Program executing source code instruction by instruction”.
e: Interpreter: Program executing source code instruction by instruction. Often supports interactive execution

q: Identify the term described as “Binary instructions directly understood by a processor”.
e: Machine language: Binary instructions directly understood by a processor. Hardware dependent

q: Identify the term described as “Programming language with abstraction from hardware details”.
e: High-level language: Programming language with abstraction from hardware details. Examples include Python and Java

q: Identify the term described as “Error or defect in software”.
e: Bug: Error or defect in software. Can cause incorrect behavior

q: Identify the term described as “Process of finding and correcting software errors”.
e: Debugging: Process of finding and correcting software errors. Uses testing and diagnostic tools

q: Identify the term described as “Interconnected devices sharing data and resources”.
e: Network: Interconnected devices sharing data and resources. Can be local or wide-area

q: Identify the term described as “Local Area Network”.
e: LAN: Local Area Network. Covers a limited area such as a building

q: Identify the term described as “Wide Area Network”.
e: WAN: Wide Area Network. Spans large geographic areas

q: Identify the term described as “Global network of interconnected networks”.
e: Internet: Global network of interconnected networks. Uses the TCP/IP protocol suite

q: Identify the term described as “Interlinked information system accessed over the Internet”.
e: World Wide Web: Interlinked information system accessed over the Internet. Uses web browsers and HTTP

q: Identify the term described as “Numerical identifier for a device on an IP network”.
e: IP address: Numerical identifier for a device on an IP network. IPv4 and IPv6 are major versions

q: Identify the term described as “Human-readable Internet name mapped to an IP address”.
e: Domain name: Human-readable Internet name mapped to an IP address. Resolved by DNS

q: Identify the term described as “Domain Name System”.
e: DNS: Domain Name System. Translates domain names into IP addresses

q: Identify the term described as “Uniform Resource Locator”.
e: URL: Uniform Resource Locator. Address identifying a resource and access method

q: Identify the term described as “Hypertext Transfer Protocol”.
e: HTTP: Hypertext Transfer Protocol. Transfers web resources

q: Identify the term described as “HTTP protected using transport-layer encryption”.
e: HTTPS: HTTP protected using transport-layer encryption. Authenticates and encrypts web communication

q: Identify the term described as “Application for accessing and displaying web content”.
e: Web browser: Application for accessing and displaying web content. Examples include Firefox and Chrome

q: Identify the term described as “Service indexing and retrieving web information”.
e: Search engine: Service indexing and retrieving web information. Responds to user queries

q: Identify the term described as “Electronic mail”.
e: Email: Electronic mail. Transfers messages over networks

q: Identify the term described as “Simple Mail Transfer Protocol”.
e: SMTP: Simple Mail Transfer Protocol. Used mainly to send email

q: Identify the term described as “Internet Message Access Protocol”.
e: IMAP: Internet Message Access Protocol. Synchronizes mail stored on a server

q: Identify the term described as “Post Office Protocol version 3”.
e: POP3: Post Office Protocol version 3. Downloads email from a server

q: Identify the term described as “On-demand access to shared computing resources over networks”.
e: Cloud computing: On-demand access to shared computing resources over networks. Includes IaaS, PaaS and SaaS

q: Identify the term described as “Infrastructure as a Service”.
e: IaaS: Infrastructure as a Service. Provides virtualized compute, storage and networking

q: Identify the term described as “Platform as a Service”.
e: PaaS: Platform as a Service. Provides application development and deployment platform

q: Identify the term described as “Software as a Service”.
e: SaaS: Software as a Service. Delivers applications over the Internet

q: Identify the term described as “Creation of virtual versions of computing resources”.
e: Virtualization: Creation of virtual versions of computing resources. Allows multiple virtual machines on one host

q: Identify the term described as “Protection of systems, networks and data”.
e: Cybersecurity: Protection of systems, networks and data. Addresses confidentiality, integrity and availability

q: Identify the term described as “Malicious software”.
e: Malware: Malicious software. Includes viruses, worms and ransomware

q: Identify the term described as “Malware that attaches to files or programs and replicates when executed”.
e: Computer virus: Malware that attaches to files or programs and replicates when executed. Often needs user action to spread

q: Identify the term described as “Self-replicating malware spreading across networks”.
e: Worm: Self-replicating malware spreading across networks. Does not require attachment to a host file

q: Identify the term described as “Malware disguised as legitimate software”.
e: Trojan horse: Malware disguised as legitimate software. Relies on deception

q: Identify the term described as “Malware encrypting or blocking data for payment”.
e: Ransomware: Malware encrypting or blocking data for payment. Backups reduce recovery impact

q: Identify the term described as “Fraudulent attempt to obtain information through deceptive messages”.
e: Phishing: Fraudulent attempt to obtain information through deceptive messages. Often impersonates trusted entities

q: Identify the term described as “System controlling network traffic according to rules”.
e: Firewall: System controlling network traffic according to rules. Can be hardware or software

q: Identify the term described as “Transformation of readable data into protected ciphertext”.
e: Encryption: Transformation of readable data into protected ciphertext. Requires a key for decryption

q: Identify the term described as “Verification of identity”.
e: Authentication: Verification of identity. Passwords and biometrics are examples

q: Identify the term described as “Determination of permitted actions after identity is established”.
e: Authorization: Determination of permitted actions after identity is established. Follows authentication

q: Identify the term described as “Copy of data kept for recovery”.
e: Backup: Copy of data kept for recovery. Should be tested and stored safely

q: Identify the term described as “Software whose source code is available under an open licence”.
e: Open-source software: Software whose source code is available under an open licence. Can be inspected and modified under licence terms

q: Identify the term described as “Software controlled under restrictive ownership licences”.
e: Proprietary software: Software controlled under restrictive ownership licences. Source code is commonly unavailable

q: Identify the term described as “American Standard Code for Information Interchange”.
e: ASCII: American Standard Code for Information Interchange. Original standard uses seven bits

q: Identify the term described as “Universal character-encoding standard”.
e: Unicode: Universal character-encoding standard. Represents scripts and symbols globally

q: Identify the term described as “Base-two number system”.
e: Binary number system: Base-two number system. Uses digits zero and one

q: Identify the term described as “Base-ten number system”.
e: Decimal number system: Base-ten number system. Uses digits zero through nine

q: Identify the term described as “Base-sixteen number system”.
e: Hexadecimal number system: Base-sixteen number system. Uses digits zero-nine and letters A-F
